summary: An excerpt from a novel (labelled 'Book 12 — part 71') describing Lexy and Houseman spending a quiet spring afternoon by a stream, where Houseman skips stones and reveals basic facts about himself: he is from Baltimore, is twenty-six, works on a cargo steamer, and turned down a family navy tradition. As they return home at sunset, Mrs. Royce sees them and concludes Houseman is the one for Lexy. Meanwhile George Grey, suffering inwardly, listens from the sitting room as Lexy introduces Houseman as Caroline Enderby's fiancé.
one_line: Lexy and Houseman share a spring afternoon by a stream, while Mrs. Royce and George Grey react to their growing bond.
key_facts: Houseman skipped stones with skill and earnest attention by the stream while Lexy watched minnows in the limpid water.
Houseman was twenty-six years old and came from Baltimore.
Houseman's father and grandfather were both in the navy, but his people wanted him to join and he refused, calling it 'Too cut and dried!'
Houseman was working on a cargo steamer and said he liked it.
Houseman had two brothers in the navy and three married sisters, and both of his parents were living.
Lexy, as a New Englander, had something to say about clam chowder, while Houseman was an authority on oysters.
The sun was setting as Lexy and Houseman turned homeward, and Houseman found nothing better to say than that he was hungry.
Lexy replied 'So am I!' and they looked at each other as if they had discovered another bond between them.
Mrs. Royce saw them from the kitchen window and concluded, 'He's the one!'
Mandy, a vegan guest, was so glad that she began making a superb chocolate cake and hummed a song about a young man on Springfield Mountain who killed a 'pesky sarpent.'
George Grey sat in the sitting room smoking and pretending to read, but never turned a page.
George Grey looked fastidiously neat, self-possessed, and a little haughty, but in spirit he was suffering horribly.
Lexy held out her hand to George Grey and searched his face with an anxious and friendly glance.
Lexy introduced Houseman as 'Caroline Enderby's fiancé.'
